name: Pi Coding Agent
description: A minimal, hackable terminal coding harness that lets developers customize their AI coding agent workflow through extensions, skills, prompt templates, and themes distributed as npm packages. Ships with powerful defaults but intentionally skips features like sub-agents and plan mode to let teams build their own workflows.
community_quotes: The npm-based package distribution is the right architectural call. Making the agent extensible through tooling developers already use for dependency management avoids the 'special plugin registry' trap
Pi is such a joy to use! It's easy, customizable, and fits my workflow perfectly. I use Pi inside my VScodium terminal with opensource models
The customizable harness angle is interesting. I think coding agents get much more useful when teams can shape the workflow around their own review habits
We're entering the era where coding agents become teammates instead of tools

name: Edgee Fallback Models
description: An agent gateway that provides automatic fallback routing for Claude Code when Anthropic is down, rate-limited, or plan caps are hit. Routes to alternative models (Kimi K2.6, Gemma, GLM, Qwen) or self-hosted options (Bedrock, Vertex, Azure) with zero code changes. Features token compression reducing costs by up to 50%.
community_quotes: Fallback models for Claude Code is exactly what's needed hitting a rate limit mid-task and losing context is painful
The auto-fallback when rate limits kick in is the part I always end up wiring by hand. Good luck with the launch!
Love the "compress" part. Most fallback tools just switch models and you lose half the context. If this works well, it could cut my AI bill in half
Smart approach to a real pain point. The rate limiting on Claude Code during peak hours has killed my flow more times than I'd like to admit

name: MashuPack
description: A developer tool that turns codebases into clean files optimized for Claude and ChatGPT consumption, helping developers prepare repository context for AI coding agents.

name: AgentRail
description: An open-source local control plane and task lifecycle layer for AI coding agents that connects agents to GitHub, Linear, and CI with structured typed events. Features per-agent scoped auth, rules-based task routing, structured CI summaries, and runs entirely locally.
community_quotes: A local control plane for coding agents is a huge win for security-conscious teams
The webhook → raw json → custom parser loop is the part of agent infra I hate most
This is a really thoughtful system, and the core idea is strong
Honestly, the babysitting part is the biggest bottleneck with coding agents right now

name: Pixcode
description: A self-hosted web UI and desktop/server control room for managing multiple AI coding agents (Claude Code, Cursor CLI, OpenAI Codex, Gemini CLI, Qwen Code, and OpenCode) with multi-agent orchestration, files, shell, Git, API keys, notifications, plugins, MCP, and theme customization.
community_quotes: A self-hosted control room for AI coding agents
